u0: No client is waiting for an order to be taken, no taken order is awaiting preparation, no prepared food is awaiting service, and no dropped food needs immediate recovery. All past obligations are currently discharged, so the agent can watch for the next client arrival or food slip and respond when it happens. The shop job is ongoing, making this a ready position rather than the end of the episode.
u1: An order has been taken and the food for it still has to be prepared at the stove; the client remains waiting. The main objective is to fetch food if necessary and prepare it while the client waits. If the carried food slips before it is prepared, recovering it on the very next step becomes an urgent additional duty.
u10: A client has arrived and is waiting to give their order, while an order already taken still needs its food prepared. The agent must eventually take the waiting client's order and also prepare food for the taken order. A slip now would add an immediate pickup duty.
u11: There are three open duties: a client is waiting to have their order taken, an order already taken still needs food prepared, and food has just slipped. The next step is critical: the agent must be holding food again or the task fails. After recovery, the waiting client's order must be taken and the other order's food prepared.
u12: One order has been taken and its food still needs to be prepared, and separately prepared food is waiting to be served. Both obligations must eventually be discharged. If food slips now, immediate pickup becomes another urgent requirement.
u13: An order still needs food prepared, prepared food is waiting to be served, and food has just slipped. The very next step must restore the agent's hold on food, or the task fails. After that recovery, the two order duties—preparing the taken order's food and serving the prepared food—remain.
u14: Food slipped from the agent's hands and was not picked up on the very next step, so the mandatory rule to hold food again immediately after a slip has been violated. This is an irreversible failure: no later pickup or service can restore successful completion.
u15: A client is waiting to have their order taken, an order already taken still awaits food preparation, and prepared food awaits service. All three obligations remain open, and the agent must eventually take the waiting order, prepare the taken order's food, and serve the prepared food. There is no immediate pickup duty unless food slips.
u16: All four kinds of duty are open: a client is waiting to order, an order already taken needs food prepared, prepared food needs serving, and food has just slipped. The next step is the most urgent—the agent must hold food again or the task fails. Once the dropped food is recovered, the order-taking, preparation, and serving duties still remain.
u2: Food has already been prepared for a waiting client, but that client has not yet been served. The agent must deliver the prepared food by serving the client. If the prepared food slips, it must first be picked up on the very next step, and then still served.
u3: Food has just slipped out of the agent's hands and no other order or preparation duty is currently outstanding. The agent must pick food up on the very next step; failing to be holding food then is an irreversible failure. After a successful pickup, there are no remaining promises unless a new client or slip creates one.
u4: An order is still waiting to be prepared, and food has just slipped, so the immediate one-step duty is to pick it up. If the agent does not hold food on the next step, the task fails. After recovery, the taken order still needs its food prepared and eventually served.
u5: Prepared food has slipped from the agent's hands, and the waiting client's order still needs to be served. The next step must be used to pick the food up; otherwise the task fails. Once recovered, the prepared food must still be delivered to the client.
u6: A client has arrived and is waiting at the counter, but their order has not yet been taken. The agent must go to the client and take the order. If food slips now, that immediate recovery duty would take priority as an additional requirement.
u7: A client is waiting to have their order taken, and there is also prepared food awaiting service. Both duties remain outstanding: take the waiting client's order and serve the prepared food. If the food slips, it must be picked up on the very next step before these can be completed.
u8: A client is waiting for their order to be taken, and food has just slipped. The immediate requirement is to hold food again on the very next step or fail. After recovering the food, the agent still needs to take the waiting client's order.
u9: A client is waiting to order, prepared food is waiting to be served, and food has just slipped. The next step must be used to pick up the dropped food; otherwise the hard requirement is broken and the task fails. If recovery succeeds, both remaining duties—taking the new order and serving the prepared food—still have to be completed.
